title: Action de Galois sur Teichmüller : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting. This page belongs to Grothendieck's combinatorial study of 'cartes' (dessins d'enfants), viewed as triangulated maps of type {0,1,∞}. The ingredients are:
- R is the set of triangles (flags). R^+ is the positively oriented ones.
- τ_i are reflections and ρ_i (written σ_i on this page) are rotations about the vertex of type i.
- R_r^{ij} is a base point on the side of r joining the vertices of types i and j (a 'midpoint').
- a_r^k is the arc inside r joining the two midpoints opposite the vertex of type k.
- λ_r^i is the arc crossing from r to a neighbouring triangle around the vertex of type i.
- Λ_r^i = λ·λ is the 'double-step' rotation of the previous page (13). The previous page's relations (14), Λ^i_r Λ^i_{τ_{i-1}r} = 1, express redundancy.

All of this is a 2-complex, dual-like to the triangulation, drawn on the punctured surface X* (X minus the vertices, the 'trous'). It yields a presentation of the fundamental groupoid of X* with many base points, one per edge-midpoint. This is the kind of explicit presentation Grothendieck needed to write down Galois and Teichmüller actions on π_1 combinatorially.

What this page does. Grothendieck fixes the vertex type 1. This is natural because in a barycentric subdivision (ρ_1^2 = 1, the previous page) type 1 plays a special role. He then simplifies the complex in two steps:
1. He eliminates the base points R_r^{0∞}, i.e. the midpoints of sides not containing a type-1 vertex, together with the arcs a_r^1 joining them.
2. He keeps the base points R_r^{ij} with {i,j} ≠ {0,∞}, and the arcs λ_r^1, Λ_r^0, Λ_r^∞ and a_r^0, a_r^∞.

The relations are the redundancy relations (14) plus one 2-cell relation per r, relation (16):
Λ^∞_{σ_1 r} (β^1_{σ_1 r})^{-1} Λ^0_r β^1_r = 1, where β^1_r = a^∞_r λ^1_r a^0_r.
This is a loop based at R_r^{∞1}. Here β^1_r is the path in r going around the type-1 corner.

Geometrically, the left margin explains the new 2-cells. The surface is tiled by 'squares', each the union of two triangles adjacent along a side of type 1, i.e. r and σ_1 r. Their corners are 'rounded' so that the tiles are star-shaped pieces avoiding the holes. Relation (16) is the boundary word of such a square.

Grothendieck observes (NB) that replacing r by σ_1 r gives an equivalent relation. Since the relation set is stable under r ↦ σ_1 r, it suffices to take r ∈ R^+ (X oriented). The upshot is a reduced presentation of π_1(X*; midpoints of type-1 sides): generators indexed by R and relations indexed by R^+ / ⟨σ_1⟩. This is essentially a van Kampen / CW-collapse computation.

The next page ('Cas IV', a figure of a chain of small circles around successive vertices) continues with other cases of this reduction.
errors: Notational inconsistency between the two forms of (16). In the first form β^1_r = a^∞_r λ^1_r a^0_r, so its inverse is (a^0_r)^{-1}(λ^1_r)^{-1}(a^∞_r)^{-1}. The second, boxed form instead writes β_r^{1,-1} as (a^∞_r)^{-1}λ^1_r(a^0_r)^{-1}, and inside the bracket for σ_1 r it appears to use a^∞ twice where a^0 is expected. These are orientation/inversion slips; the intended relation is clearly the boundary word of the square r ∪ σ_1 r.

The equation number (14) is reused: it numbers the retained base points on this page, but also the redundancy relations of the previous page that are invoked here. (16) is likewise used for two displays.
The superscript on Λ in the boxed (16) ('Λ^{1∞}') looks like a slip for Λ^∞.

ideas.what: Presentation of the fundamental groupoid of a punctured surface carrying a dessin/triangulated map, with base points at edge midpoints, generators being local arcs (rotations around vertices, crossings of triangles) and relations from 2-cells
ideas.modern_name: Combinatorial presentation of π_1 / fundamental groupoid of the punctured surface of a dessin (cartographic group, van Kampen for a CW-complex)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Classical combinatorial topology (van Kampen, Reidemeister); in the dessins setting Grothendieck, Malgoire–Voisin, Jones–Singerman
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme discusses cartes, cartographic groups and fundamental groupoids with base points at many points, but not this explicit presentation

ideas.what: Reduction of the complex by distinguishing the vertex type 1 (barycentric case): removing midpoints of {0,∞}-sides and tiling the punctured surface by 'squares' r ∪ σ_1 r with rounded corners avoiding the punctures; relations indexed by R^+/σ_1
ideas.modern_name: Collapsing a CW-structure / choosing a quadrangulation dual to the map (edges of the dessin as quadrilaterals)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Standard; the quadrilateral picture of a map's edges is folklore in map theory (e.g. Tutte; Lando–Zvonkin)

deep.surprise_reason: This is a careful but routine combinatorial-topology computation: an explicit groupoid presentation for the punctured surface of a dessin, reduced by collapsing cells. It is useful scaffolding for the Galois/Teichmüller program, but contains no new result or unexplored connection beyond what dessins/van Kampen techniques give.
transcription_corrections: Header 'Suite 1' is probably just 'Suite'; the page-internal number is 9.
'un indice des fusions' is likely 'un indice des sommets' (or 'un type'), i.e. fixing a vertex type, namely 1.
'(cas présent ou cas où...)' may read '(cas presque ... / cas où la triangulation est barycentrique, donc où 1 joue un rôle particulier!)'.
'∫ R_r^{i,j}' is a left brace '{ R_r^{i,j}', not an integral sign.

Margin 'rouages par des carrés (dont deux connectés...)' is more plausibly 'pavage par des carrés (dont deux adjacents par un côté de type 1), par des "arrondis", en forme de ... des triangles évitant les trous'.
'(où X orientée)' should read '(car X orientée)'.
In the second (16), the inner bracket should probably read (a^0_{σ_1 r})^{-1}... / a^∞ λ^1 a^0, consistent with β^1.
